principles: Physical plausibility qualifies a source; it is not a target to force-match.
Texture information is preserved: clipping and contrast are measured per transform; flattened detail fails.
Correct sources are preferred over aggressive correction; travertine never ships under a marble identity.
Final rendered behaviour is validated under neutral and grazing light, across representative scenes and both supported renderers.
Corrections are reproducible: source bytes retained, every transform and hash recorded.

outcome.legacy: The six pre-F entries stay resolvable with legacy: true and leave the creator shelf; new shapes, candidates and native definitions default to plaster-painted and the room portal to metal-brass-satin; generated walls and ceilings without a Finish keep the plaster-warm scalars (they bind no maps), and texturing them is left to a later look slice.

qualificationMethod: Offline qualification sheets: each ladder level magnified to the 1440p design-distance screen density (surface 1.5 m = 850 px/m, object 0.8 m = 1595 px/m), colour × lit normal under a grazing key, beside a 2×2 tile of the 512 level for seams and repeat. Where a level's magnification is below 1 the sheet sampler has no mip prefilter, so differences above that level are aliasing a GPU would not show and are discounted. Agent judgement; the owner retains final visual acceptance.

reproducibility.result: all 16 sets re-derived from the retained sources with identical bytes

renderGap.found: The first rendered board showed the metal sets (normal + ORM, no colour map) on the flat fallback: loadMaterialTextures, loadEffectiveTextures and CatalogueMaterial treated a missing colour map as failure even when the entry binds none.
renderGap.fix: A set without a bound colour slot is ready on the structure maps it carries; a set that binds a colour map still falls back when that map fails.
renderGap.test: apps/editor/tests/lib/render/resources/texture-store.test.ts — binds a map-less set by the structure maps it carries (S8 F metals)

scenes.coverage: The three vignettes place all 21 curated entries; painted brick and white marble positions take plaster and travertine under their own identities.

observations: Every cell settled with no failed material on both renderers; WebGL2 frames match WebGPU frames by eye.
Studio v2 is deliberately dim for diffuse surfaces (the owner-approved 0.2x radiance scale serves the highlight gate); judgements compare entries within the rig, not absolute brightness.
Metals read as reflective under studio and as dark, highlight-only surfaces under grazing (which has no reflection map), as expected.
Grazing shows relief on plaster, tile grout, brick, carpet and leather; no entry reads flattened.
Painted plaster keeps its mottling after the recorded gain (0.5% clipped, contrast preserved).
Travertine banding continues across the 1.2 m repeat with no visible seam (colour seam ratio 1.094, normal 1.137 at the qualified level).
Terrazzo reads as a warm-grey aggregate, true to the source; it is not recoloured.
Herringbone parquet holds block edges at 2K; linen weave and leather grain resolve at 0.9 m.

notes.tileReference: The Physically Based porcelain reference (#e0e0dd) reads 1.272x darker than the glazed white tile source. A glazed ceramic is brighter than unglazed porcelain body, so the reference is judged not fully applicable; the source is kept and the entry factor reaches the design target without clipping.
